LING 100.title: Introduction to Language and Linguistics
LING 100.description: Study of language as a universal and uniquely human cognitive system: What universals do all languages share and how do languages differ? An investigation of sound systems, word-building, grammatical principles, language change, dialect variation, language acquisition, neurolinguistics. Recommended but not required for an honours, major, or minor in linguistics or speech sciences.

LING 101.title: Languages of the World
LING 101.description: A survey of the linguistic map of the world, examining how languages are genetically classified and how different languages evolve. Principles underlying different writing systems and the decipherment of historical documents. Issues of languages in contact, minority language endangerment, language death and the role of English as a world language. Recommended but not required for an honours, major, or minor in linguistics or speech sciences.

LING 140.title: Challenging Language Myths
LING 140.description: Critical consideration of a broad range of commonly held beliefs about language and its relation to the brain and cognition, learning, society, change and evolution. Note. This is an elective course that does not fulfill writing requirements in any faculty or the literature requirement in the Faculty of Arts.

LING 142.title: Language in the Age of AI
LING 142.description: Examines the impact of generative AI, large language models, and virtual assistants on human communication. Includes evolving language trends, ethics, and applications like speech recognition, text-to-speech, and machine translation. No computational or programming background required.

LING 170.title: Introduction to How to Learn a Language
LING 170.description: Skills and strategies for second language acquisition, through the foundations of pronunciation, vocabulary, grammar, and pragmatics, connected to the practical, social, and personal challenges of language learning.

LING 200.title: Linguistic Theory and Analysis I
LING 200.description: Introduction to phonetics and phonology; training in the identification and production of speech sounds; principles and methods for describing and writing the sound system of a language; phonological theory with reference to selected languages; the interface between phonology and morphology. Analytical practice and seminar discussion.

LING 201.title: Linguistic Theory and Analysis II
LING 201.description: Introduction to grammatical analysis; morphology, syntax, semantics; synchronic analysis and description with illustrations from various languages. Analytical practice and seminar discussion.

LING 209.title: Clinical Topics in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences
LING 209.description: Introduction to speech and hearing sciences, with emphasis on the clinical perspectives of audiology and speech pathology.

LING 222.title: Language Acquisition
LING 222.description: Audition and speech perception, phonological organization, word learning, syntax, and pragmatics.

LING 242.title: Computational Tools for Linguistic Analysis
LING 242.description: Practical skills for analyzing language using the Python programming language and relevant packages.
LING 242.prerequisiteText: One of LING 100, LING 101, LING 140, LING 170, LING 200, LING 201, ENGL 330, ENGL 331
notes: Recommended: LING 201 and CPSC 103 or CPSC 110 (or other programming experience)

LING 270.title: Introduction to Studies in Second Language Acquisition
LING 270.description: Linguistic systems that learners of an additional language develop as they approximate towards the target language, and key questions about what this 'interlanguage' system reveals about how we learn languages.
LING 270.prerequisiteText: One of LING 100, LING 101, LING 140, LING 170

LING 300.title: Studies in Grammar
LING 300.description: Introduction to syntactic analysis and theory, with emphasis on description and analysis of data from a wide variety of languages.

LING 308.title: The Languages of Africa
LING 308.description: Linguistic survey of the languages of Africa, including typological and historical connections between languages, individual and comparative surveys of sound systems, word structures, sentence structures, semantics, and sociolinguistic properties of a representative selection of languages.

LING 311.title: Studies in Phonology
LING 311.description: Introduction to phonological analysis and theory, with a strong emphasis on description and analysis of data from a wide variety of languages.

LING 313.title: Introduction to Linguistic Phonetics and Speech Science
LING 313.description: The articulatory and acoustic properties of speech production and perception, including practice in phonetic transcription, instrumental recording, and the analysis of normal speech.

LING 314.title: Instrumental Phonetics
LING 314.description: Physiological and/or acoustic phonetics. Focus on experimental methods and analysis techniques. Topics may include: source-filter theory; spectral and temporal acoustic analysis, inter-articulator timing and motor coordination.

LING 315.title: Sociolinguistics
LING 315.description: The systematic study of language as a social phenomenon.

LING 319.title: Historical Linguistics
LING 319.description: How and why languages change over time, and how languages can be grouped into families based on historical relationships. Methods of comparative and internal reconstruction of phonological, morphological, syntactic, semantic change. Social factors in language change. Not offered every year.

LING 327.title: Introduction to Semantics
LING 327.description: The analysis and theory of linguistic meaning with emphasis on formal techniques for semantic analysis and their application to empirical phenomena in language, including pragmatics.

LING 333.title: Research Methods for Linguistics
LING 333.description: Research methods used in linguistics and speech science. Emphasis on scientific reasoning, critical thinking, experimental design, and the ethics and methods of linguistic data-collection.

LING 342.title: Computational Models of Language
LING 342.description: A re-examination of major areas of linguistics from a computational perspective, including popular formalisms and algorithms associated with morphology, syntax, semantics, and discourse.
LING 342.prerequisiteText: LING 242 and one of LING 201, ENGL 331 and one of STAT 200, STAT 203, STAT 251, STAT 302, MATH 302, PSYC 218

LING 345.title: Pragmatics
LING 345.description: Selected topics in pragmatics and information structure, including variations in their cross-linguistic expression and the corresponding influence of sentence form on context.
LING 345.prerequisiteText: One of LING 201, ENGL 331, PHIL 220, PHIL 222

LING 405.title: Morphology
LING 405.description: Analytic and theoretical consideration of the interrelation of word formation, sound patterning, and meaningful sentence structure. Not offered every year.

LING 415.title: Language Across Time, Geography, and Society
LING 415.description: A cross-linguistic exploration of language change, discussing theories, data, and methods. Topics can include change across historical time periods, lifespan; change across regions, within areas; change due to language contact and other social and cultural factors.
LING 415.prerequisiteText: One of LING 319, LING 315, LING 445, ENGL 318, ENGL 319, ENGL 324 and two of LING 300, LING 311, LING 313, LING 327

LING 420.title: Introduction to Linguistics
LING 420.description: General background to linguistic studies; the different approaches to the analysis of languages; synchronic and diachronic linguistics; phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics. Not available for credit toward a Major or Honours program in Linguistics.

LING 425.title: Advanced Semantics
notes: A basic introduction to syntax is recommended (e.g., LING_V 100, LING_V 201, or ENGL_V 331).

LING 430.title: Honours Seminar in Linguistics
LING 430.description: Research papers on general linguistic topics to be read and discussed.

LING 431.title: Field Methods I
LING 431.description: Elicitation, transcription, organization, and analysis of linguistic data from a native speaker of a language not commonly studied. Practical experience in the use of fieldwork equipment.

LING 432.title: Field Methods II
LING 432.description: Elicitation, transcription, organization, and analysis of linguistic data from a native speaker of a language not commonly studied. Practical experience in the use of fieldwork equipment.

LING 433.title: Indigenous Languages of the Americas
LING 433.description: Survey of the Indigenous languages of the Americas. Genetic classification and areal similarities. Structures of representative languages. The present status of Indigenous languages in the Americas, language shift, and reclamation. (Note: this course is not necessarily offered every year.)

LING 436.title: Community-based Language Research
LING 436.description: Research methods and partnerships, ethical paradigms, the social, cultural and historical context of language research, and the relation of language research to pedagogy, policy and planning.

LING 440.title: Language as a Social Instrument
LING 440.description: Language as a tool that shapes and is shaped by technology, media, politics and power relations in society. Considers multiple levels of linguistic structure from a cross-linguistic perspective.

LING 447.title: Topics in Linguistics
LING 447.description: A capstone course for Linguistics and Speech Sciences majors, normally taken after three years of study. Individual sections will differ substantially; see online Course List for detailed descriptions and prerequisites. May be repeated for credit when content is different.

LING 448.title: Directed Studies
LING 448.description: Supervisor and topic chosen by mutual agreement between student and Linguistics faculty member. Department Advisor approval is required.

LING 451.title: Acquisition of Phonology
LING 451.description: Development of the phonological system in typical first language acquisition from the perspective of diverse linguistic topics. Phonetic transcription of child speech.

LING 452.title: Acquisition of Syntax
LING 452.description: Central issues in the first language acquisition of syntax, including early lexical and semantic development, acquisition of morphology, and syntactic development (e.g., word order, questions).

LING 469.title: Clinical Topics in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences
LING 469.description: Introduction to speech and hearing sciences with emphasis on the clinical perspectives of audiology and speech pathology.

LING 502.title: Formal Foundations of Syntax & Semantics
LING 502.description: Conceptual underpinnings of the study of sentence structure and meaning; core issues in syntax and semantics; the place of syntax and semantics in a model of grammar; interface issues.

LING 505.title: Issues in Morphological Theory and Analysis
LING 505.description: Morphology from both historical and theoretical perspectives.

LING 507.title: Formal Foundations of Phonetics & Phonology
LING 507.description: Conceptual underpinnings of the study of speech sounds; core issues in phonetics and phonology; the place of phonetics and phonology in a model of grammar; interface issues.

LING 508.title: Phonetic Theory & Analysis
LING 508.description: Discussion and critical analysis of current issues in linguistic phonetics; instrumental analysis.

LING 510.title: Phonological Theory and Analysis
LING 510.description: Discussion and critical analysis of current issues in phonological theory.

LING 512.title: Topics in Phonetics & Phonology
LING 512.description: Advanced topics in phonetics and phonology; in-depth analysis of specific issues and problems.

LING 519.title: Problems in Comparative and Historical Linguistics

LING 520.title: Syntactic Theory and Analysis
LING 520.description: Discussion and critical analysis of current issues in syntactic theory.

LING 522.title: Topics in Syntax and Semantics
LING 522.description: Advanced topics in syntax and semantics; in-depth analysis of specific issues and problems.

LING 525.title: Semantic Theory and Analysis
LING 525.description: Discussion and critical analysis of current issues in semantic theory.

LING 530.title: Linguistic Problems in a Special Area

LING 538.title: Seminar on Language Acquisition in Children
LING 538.description: Linguistic analysis of data from children learning a first language. Intensive examination of a topic that will vary each year dealing with advanced research into phonological, syntactic, and semantic aspects of language acquisition.

LING 546.title: Directed Reading in Topics related to Linguistics

LING 560.title: Managing and Preserving Linguistic Data
LING 560.description: Theory and practice of research data management and preservation with an emphasis on linguistic and language data.
